scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §§4-5 (health checks in metrics but no request-completed log; /metrics text format with no-store); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-001
preconditions: A file-mode Observer with full process identity is mounted on an HTTP mux with a /healthz route and a normal API route.
The metrics endpoint is served by the same Observer.
scenarios.input: GET /healthz (204) and GET /api/admin/forms (200) through the Observer middleware, then GET /metrics.
scenarios.action: Inspect logs.jsonl, the local counter/histogram snapshot and the /metrics response headers.
scenarios.expected_result: Both routes increment zubrium_http_server_requests_total and zubrium_http_server_duration_seconds; only the API route emits http request completed, /metrics returns text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8 with Cache-Control: no-store.
scenarios.expected_state: Health checks leave no completion log line; both routes remain fully counted and correlated.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §5 (409 expectedRevision span/log contract); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-002
preconditions: A file-mode Observer wraps an authenticated PATCH route that returns 409 conflict.
The request carries Authorization, Cookie, a form body and a raw query value.
scenarios.input: PATCH /api/admin/forms/form-42?form=do-not-leak with a conflicting revision, a credential-bearing header set and a form-values body.
scenarios.action: Read the emitted http.server span, completion log and all three signal files.
scenarios.expected_result: Business status is 409; span carries http.status_code=409, span.status=error, outcome=error and typed error attributes; the log is warn/error with the same trace_id; no secret, cookie, form value or raw query value appears in any signal.
scenarios.expected_state: Telemetry records use the route template and stay free of request bodies and credentials; the business conflict is unchanged.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §§3.1, 5 (correlation headers, route template, mandatory identity); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-003
preconditions: A file-mode Observer with presentation identity handles GET /api/admin/forms.
The request has a valid W3C traceparent and a raw query string with sensitive values.
scenarios.action: Compare response correlation headers with the emitted log and http.server span; scan all signal files for query leakage.
scenarios.expected_result: Status 200, X-Request-ID equals the child span_id, X-Trace-ID equals the incoming trace_id; log and span carry the same presentation module/component/operation identity and the route template; the raw query and file ID never appear in telemetry.
scenarios.expected_state: One trace correlates response, log and span without high-cardinality or credential leakage.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §§3.1, 4 (worker task span and worker metrics); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-004
preconditions: A file-mode Observer receives the trusted worker boundary identity and emits worker.task metrics with low-cardinality labels.
scenarios.input: A completed worker.media Operation named worker.task with operation ID engine.media/derivative/v1 and a task-ID span attribute, followed by zubrium_worker_task_total and zubrium_worker_task_duration_seconds observations.
scenarios.action: Read spans.jsonl and metrics.jsonl and compare identity, outcome and exemplar trace IDs.
scenarios.expected_result: The worker.task span and both worker metric samples carry module.kind=worker, the actual module.id, component.id, operation.id and outcome; identity is not replaced by composition or bus; task IDs stay out of metric labels.
scenarios.expected_state: The worker span and metrics share one trace while keeping metric series low-cardinality.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §§2.1, 3.1 (three JSONL files, mandatory fields, rotation bounds); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-005
preconditions: File mode uses a 1024-byte limit and max_files=2 in an isolated temporary directory.
HTTP and bus calls have completed before rotation is forced.
scenarios.input: One HTTP request, one bus.dispatch span with a counter, then 25 log records large enough to rotate logs.jsonl repeatedly.
scenarios.action: Parse every active and rotated JSONL line, check mandatory fields and trace correlation, enumerate rotated files and verify the last record is in the active file.
scenarios.expected_result: logs.jsonl, spans.jsonl and metrics.jsonl exist; every line is a JSON object with UTC RFC3339Nano timestamp, signal and the §3.1 identity/trace set; .1 is created, indices never exceed max_files and the active record survives rotation.
scenarios.expected_state: Rotation removes only oldest indices; the process keeps writing valid records and the HTTP trace is present in all three signals.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §2.2 (OTLP to Collector/OpenObserve, three signal pipelines); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-006
preconditions: A disposable OTLP/HTTP Collector and OpenObserve stack is reachable.
OBS_TEST_OTEL_ENDPOINT names the Collector base URL; OBS_TEST_OQ_SEARCH_URL is a query URL template with a trace-id placeholder and optional {signal} selector.
scenarios.input: One HTTP request, one worker.task operation and one bus.dispatch with a shared trace ID in otel mode, then three stream queries by trace ID after flush.
scenarios.action: Export through the real OTLP SDK and query the logs, traces and metrics streams in OpenObserve.
scenarios.expected_result: All three streams contain the same trace ID with service.name, deployment.profile, module/component/operation identity and the expected signal names/metrics; debug exporter evidence is available for accepted batches.
scenarios.expected_state: Export is asynchronous and does not change the HTTP/business result; no credential is present in headers beyond the environment-provided values.
scenarios.blocker: Изолированный стек поднимается (проверено: OTLP/HTTP :14318 и OpenObserve :15080 доступны, Collector'ом приняты логи/трейсы/метрики), но исполняемый контракт подтеста ожидает один неаутентифицированный GET-поиск с подстановкой {signal}. OpenObserve v1.1.2 требует аутентифицированный POST /api/default/_search с query{sql,start_time,end_time} и отдельные stream'ы для каждой метрики; адаптация test harness к этому API не выполнена. Переменные OBS_TEST_OTEL_ENDPOINT и OBS_TEST_OQ_SEARCH_URL не заданы, поэтому три потока сигналов и debug exporter не проверены; подтест честно t.Skip.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §§5-6 (W3C traceparent validation and root fallback); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-007
preconditions: A file-mode Observer wraps GET /api/admin/forms and accepts a per-request traceparent header.
scenarios.input: Short trace ID, non-hex trace ID, zero span ID and one valid 00-form traceparent with a sampled flag; each sent as a separate request.
scenarios.action: Compare response trace headers and child spans with the incoming headers; scan logs for tracing errors.
scenarios.expected_result: Every invalid header is ignored: status 200, new nonzero root trace, no tracing error log. The valid header preserves the incoming trace_id in the child span and records the incoming span_id as parent_span_id.
scenarios.expected_state: No request is rejected because of trace context and no span inherits a malformed or zero identifier.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §§2.2, 6 (Collector outage, async bounded export, recovery); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-008
preconditions: A disposable product stack in otel mode is available with a running Collector and a controllable outage endpoint.
OBS_TEST_OTEL_ENDPOINT, OBS_TEST_OTEL_FAILURE_ENDPOINT and OBS_TEST_OQ_SEARCH_URL are configured.
scenarios.input: HTTP and worker calls with an unreachable OTLP endpoint, then the same calls with the live endpoint and a query for the recovery trace ID.
scenarios.action: Measure business status and shutdown duration during the outage, then verify that export resumes for the recovered endpoint.
scenarios.expected_result: HTTP/bus/worker results and process lifetime do not depend on telemetry; shutdown is bounded by timeout; after recovery the trace is present in the telemetry sink.
scenarios.expected_state: Lost batches are an honest limitation of the run; no business result or durable state changes during telemetry failure.
scenarios.blocker: Изолированный стек Collector+OpenObserve поднимается, но для OBS-008 нужен дополнительно управляемый отказ Collector и совместимый с OpenObserve v1.1.2 поиск (аутентифицированный POST /_search с query{sql,start_time,end_time} и отдельными stream'ами метрик), чего исполняемый контракт подтеста не поддерживает. Переменные OBS_TEST_OTEL_ENDPOINT, OBS_TEST_OTEL_FAILURE_ENDPOINT и OBS_TEST_OQ_SEARCH_URL не заданы, поэтому доступность продукта и возобновление экспорта не проверены; подтест честно t.Skip.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §3.2 (typed attributes, key/value redaction, cache-correlation keys); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-009
preconditions: A file-mode Observer with full identity receives typed attributes from an untrusted boundary.
scenarios.input: Sensitive keys (token, cookie, authorization, body, form, query, cache.key, file.id, principal.id, url, locale, user.agent, e-mail/phone/user name), credential-shaped values, a visitor e-mail under a safe key, and an over-long control-character value.
scenarios.action: Construct typed attributes, emit log/counter/span, inspect all signal files and the /metrics snapshot.
scenarios.expected_result: Sensitive keys and all integer variants are dropped; Bearer/Basic/JWT/cookie/token values and visitor e-mail are redacted; strings are bounded and control characters removed; metric labels contain no rejected key or secret value.
scenarios.expected_state: No PII, credential, cache key, file ID or principal ID reaches logs, spans, metrics or the local Prometheus snapshot.

scenarios.source: spec/observability/SPEC-observability.md §6 (parallel requests, single End, graceful shutdown); tests/ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md Observability criterion OBS-010
preconditions: A file-mode Observer handles 12 concurrent requests with distinct traceparent headers and opens one extra component.lifecycle span.
scenarios.input: Parallel HTTP requests through the middleware, a double End on one span, bounded Close, and a late End plus counter write after Close.
scenarios.action: Verify per-trace span counts and span IDs, shutdown duration and whether signal files change after shutdown.
scenarios.expected_result: Each request has exactly one span with its own trace_id/span_id and no mixed identity; double End writes one span; Close returns within the timeout; no span or metric sample is written after Close and business results remain unchanged.
scenarios.expected_state: Concurrent traces stay isolated and shutdown is terminal for the file backend.
